title: Three on a Track
statement: Three runners start at the same moment from the same point of a circular track, and each runs at a constant speed. The first runs anticlockwise at $4$ laps per hour, the second runs clockwise at $5$ laps per hour, and the third runs anticlockwise at $10$ laps per hour. Let $t$ be the time in minutes since the start. For how many values of $t$ with $0 < t \le 60$ are at least two of the runners at the same point of the track?
hints: Measure each runner's position in laps, anticlockwise from the start. Two runners are at the same point exactly when their positions differ by a whole number of laps.

Use relative speeds. After $h$ hours the runners are $4h$, $-5h$ and $10h$ laps from the start, so the first and second, the first and third, and the second and third are together exactly when $9h$, $6h$ and $15h$ are whole numbers. Count each pair's meetings, then look for moments counted more than once.
If two of the pairs are together at the same moment, all three runners are together then. That happens exactly when $3h$ is a whole number, and each such moment appears in all three pair counts.
solution: After $h$ hours the runners are $4h$, $-5h$ and $10h$ laps anticlockwise from the start. So the first and second, the first and third, and the second and third are together exactly when $9h$, $6h$ and $15h$ are integers, which for $0 < h \le 1$ happens $9 + 6 + 15 = 30$ times. If two pairs are together then all three runners are, so only meetings of all three are counted more than once, each three times. These need $9h$ and $6h$ to be integers, so $3h = 9h - 6h$ is an integer, and conversely; that gives $h = \frac{1}{3}, \frac{2}{3}, 1$. The answer is $30 - 2 \cdot 3 = 24$.
